What is the total surface area of the rectangular prism above if it is $4\,\text{cm}$ long, $3\,\text{cm}$ wide, and $3\,\text{cm}$ tall?
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's consider the net of our plank.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13986308/assets/98eb9b74a15ad1cad75974496a370fb9b9b28f7ff57bc319500fcd31492216d3.png)

$$

$$

From the diagram, we have squares and rectangles.

The rectangles are $4\,\text{cm}$ long and $3\,\text{cm}$ high. So, the area of one rectangle is:

$$
\text{Area of the rectangle}=4\times 3=12\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.
$$

The squares has the side equal to $3\,\text{cm}.$ Hence, the area of one square is:

$$
\text{Area of the square}=3\times 3=9\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.
$$

Finally, the surface area of the rectangular prism consists of $4$ rectangles and $2$ squares. 

Therefore, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =4\times (\text{Area of the rectangle})+2\times (\text{Area of the square}) \\  & =4\times 12+2\times 9 \\  & =48+18 \\  & =66\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's consider the net of our box.

 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13986308/assets/c35bb0f7b049baa569a06532b516436afaf310e28870cfbd4790467d36e54809.png)

From the diagram, we have squares and rectangles.

The rectangles are $4\,\text{m}$ long and $1\,\text{m}$ high. So, the area of one rectangle is:

$$
\text{Area of the rectangle}=4\times 1=4\,{\text{m}}^{2}.
$$

The squares has the side equal to $1\,\text{m}.$ Hence, the area of one square is:

$$
\text{Area of the square}=1\times 1=1\,{\text{m}}^{2}.
$$

Finally, the surface area of the box consists of $4$ rectangles and $2$ squares. 

Therefore, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =4\times (\text{Area of the rectangle})+2\times (\text{Area of the square}) \\  & =4\times 4+2\times 1 \\  & =16+2 \\  & =18\,{\text{m}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

A gardening company is making metal spikes from the net shown above. What is the total surface area of the spike?
questions.worked_solution:
The net shown corresponds to a rectangular pyramid. The surface area of our pyramid consists of $1$ square (base) and $4$ triangles (side faces). 

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =1\times (\text{Area of the base})+4\times (\text{Area of the side}) \\  & =1\times 12+4\times 6 \\  & =12+24 \\  & =36\,{\text{in}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

A company produces a chocolate bar that comes in an triangular-prism-shaped box. In the figure, the areas of some of the faces are displayed in a net of the prism. What is the total surface area of the box?
questions.worked_solution:
The surface area of our prism consists of $2$ triangles (base and top) and $3$ rectangles (central and side faces). 

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =2\times (\text{Area of the base})+2\times (\text{Area of the side faces}) \\  & +1\times (\text{Area of the central face}) \\  & =2\times 36+2\times 72+108 \\  & =72+144+108 \\  & =324\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Jill unfolds a cardboard box and obtains a net shown above. What is the total surface area of the box?
questions.worked_solution:
The net shown corresponds to a rectangular prism. The surface area of our prism consists of $2$ squares (base and top) and $4$ rectangles (side faces). 

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =2\times (\text{Area of the base})+4\times (\text{Area of the side}) \\  & =2\times 360+4\times 420 \\  & =720+1\,680 \\  & =2\,400\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
